harnessDiscovery.behavior: scaffoldLeafDescriptor: dual payload-schema convention accepted interchangeably — schemaCandidates array tries '🧬️schema/<canonical-json-filename>' then flat '🔣️.schema.json' beside the leaf, first existsSync() match wins. No single source of truth for where a mutation's payload schema physically lives.

rustTypeIndex: repo-wide walkDirectories(repoRoot, ...) scan of every .rs file (except excluded test paths), indexing pub struct newtypes, pub type aliases, composite pub struct bodies (brace-matched), #[serde(tag=...)] tagged enums, and fieldless pub enums — all keyed by BARE NAME with no scope qualification. This is the mechanism payload-schema derivation depends on.

resolveSnapshot (inside derivePayloadSchema, set-snapshot case): when a composite struct name is ambiguous (declared in multiple files), picks the definition whose file path shares the LONGEST COMMON PATH-PREFIX with the mutation leaf's owner path — a nearest-parent heuristic, first of three near-identical call sites.

nearest() helper inside derivePayloadSchema's resolve(): identical longest-common-path-prefix heuristic applied to ambiguous ENUM names via the placedEnums map (second call site of the same mechanism).

resolve() inside derivePayloadSchema (general struct case): identical longest-common-path-prefix heuristic applied to ambiguous COMPOSITE STRUCT names via the placed map (third call site of the same mechanism — 'Rust resolves by module path; so does this').

policyFindSchemaDeclaration: scans a schema leaf file for every matching declaration; if the expected type name (from a hardcoded prefix table or a derived config type) is found among them, returns it, but if NOT found, silently falls back to returning the FIRST declaration in the file rather than failing — a positional fallback that can mask a naming mismatch as a shape mismatch instead.

resolveSchemaFacetKind: infers whether a 🧬️schema/ directory is kind '🧬️data' or '📜️interface' by checking which kind's normative-format canonical filename ALREADY EXISTS on disk in that directory (first schemaFacetKinds entry whose normative file is present wins), defaulting to '🧬️data' if neither is found. Kind is inferred from current file layout rather than declared by the owner.

oracleHostPackagesFor: 'walking up to the nearest contributor' — filters registry.contributions by owner===entry.owner OR owner.startsWith(entry.owner+'/'), i.e. an ancestor-prefix match rather than an exact scope match. Lower-risk than the rustTypeIndex heuristics (bounded to registered contributions) but still a prefix-walk rather than an explicit binding.

buildCasePlan: 'A case is scoped by the manifest whose owner it lives under, walking up to the nearest one' — same ancestor-prefix-match pattern as above, applied to resolving a test case's owning mutation manifest. Explicitly documented as returning null (not a guess) when no owning manifest is found, which is safer than the rustTypeIndex heuristics but still a walk-up rather than an explicit id reference.

resolveFixtures — CONTRAST CASE, not a heuristic: fixture URIs (shared://, local://, asset://) are resolved by an EXPLICIT scheme against exact owner/case fixture directories, no shadowing, no nearest-dir search, path-escape-guarded, digest-pinned. This is the pattern the ticket's 'fixtures bind explicitly to exports' goal should generalize, not a discovery mechanism to remove.

vscodeLaunchJson.namingConvention: Emoji-prefixed segments <verb-emoji>verb<noun-emoji>noun<detail-emoji>detail (e.g. 📦️generate🧩️taxonomy📊️census), every entry is {"name", "type": "node-terminal", "request": "launch", "command": "bun nx run workspace:<target>" (or "<project>:<target>"), "cwd": "${workspaceFolder}", "presentation": {"group", "order"}}. Groups seen: 0_dev, 1_keyboard, 2_mouse, 3_dev, 4_build, 4_gate, 5_publish. `order` is a float so new entries insert between existing ones (e.g. 209, 209.1, 209.15, 209.2, 209.3) without renumbering siblings. A new schema/taxonomy dev command belongs in group 4_build (or 4_gate for verification-only ⚖️gate* entries), placed immediately after the sibling verify-taxonomy-*/clean-taxonomy-* block, using the next available fractional order.

extensionPoints.location: FacetLeaves struct (130-138: rust/typescript/graphql/json_schema/proto fields), ArtifactSchemaDescriptor struct (166-172: id + 4 fixed FacetLeaves fields artifact/snapshot/diff/mutations), registration + dedup (register_artifact_schema_descriptor[s]/preflight_artifact_schema_descriptors, 317-347, backed by with_artifact_schema_registry's by_id: HashMap<&'static str, ArtifactSchemaDescriptor> at line 196)
extensionPoints.why: ArtifactSchemaDescriptor.id is ALREADY a dotted scope identity (verified example: "s.trinity.jack" in ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🔱️trinity/🗿️artifacts/🔌️jack/🏅️standards/🔖️1/🪆️subsets/✳️any/🧬️schema/🦀️.rs:203), and id-collision-with-differing-body is already a hard registration error. What's MISSING is the export-id dimension: FacetLeaves hard-codes exactly 5 fixed format fields for exactly 4 fixed facet names (artifact/snapshot/diff/mutations) — no arbitrary named export beyond those 4, no per-facet multiplicity. Extending this to a keyed collection (e.g. exports: BTreeMap<&'static str, FacetLeaves>) is the most direct path from today's mechanism to the ticket's target model — prefer this over inventing a parallel type.
